Forecast Discussion

High pressure to our north and a storm well off the Carolina coast control the week. The air between them is the driest we have measured this fall, and it stays that way through the weekend. Dry air heats fast under the sun and cools fast at night, so valleys drop far below the ridgetops every night. Frost is possible each night in the protected valleys.

Tuesday is the warmest day of the stretch. The air aloft is a few degrees milder than Monday, and the sun does the rest. A northeast breeze picks up on the ridgetops. Wednesday is sunny and a notch cooler as the coastal storm pulls away.

Thursday stays sunny and mild. Cooler air drops in from the north Thursday night with no front to mark it. Friday is the cool day of the week, mostly sunny, with a few morning clouds banked against the east side of the mountains.

A strong high settles over us Saturday and Sunday. Saturday morning is the coldest of the week. Afternoons recover under full sun. A few clouds drift in late Monday.

When will we see any rain again? There is no significant rain in sight for the rest of October.
